title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Rule on the Full-Time Hours Threshold for a Supplemental Correction
content:
**(1)** For a supplemental correction on an Unemployment Benefit Claims record, the full-time hours threshold applied to the corrected week is 36 hours (the reduced-hours threshold) when the separation recorded on the claim is reduced hours.

**(2)** It is 34 hours (the recall threshold) when the separation is not reduced hours and the claim records a definite recall date falling within the recall window of 56 calendar days after the handling date: on or after the handling date and no more than 56 days after it.

**(3)** Any other supplemental correction uses the program's full-time hours threshold.

## Conditions in combination

| Separation recorded on the claim | Definite recall date recorded | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| Reduced hours | Any | 36 hours |
| Any other separation | 0 to 56 days after the handling date | 34 hours |
| Any other separation | More than 56 days after the handling date, already passed, or none | The program's full-time hours threshold |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

| Separation | Recall date | Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| Lack of work | 56 days after the handling date | 34 hours |
| Lack of work | 57 days after the handling date | The program's threshold |
| Reduced hours | 10 days after the handling date | 36 hours |
